episode.title: Resolve extension uninstall requests by installed name or recorded source
episode.before: At parent commit 0534ca74d4e67b00ed51e9f8bf568efc3ecaf834, uninstallExtension treated its argument strictly as an extension name. It required an exact case-sensitive match against installed.config.name, rejected source URLs or paths even when recorded in installation metadata, and then used the supplied argument directly for enablement removal, storage deletion, and uninstall telemetry. The CLI likewise described the positional argument only as an extension name.
episode.after: At commit 2d406ffc755f79dc903c6993aae03150e1678dc0, the uninstall boundary accepts an identifier that may be either the configured extension name or installMetadata.source. It searches loaded user extensions using case-insensitive equality, safely skips absent metadata, resolves a match to the canonical configured name, and uses that canonical name for enablement removal, directory deletion, and telemetry. The CLI advertises name or source path input. Unknown identifiers, including source identifiers for installations without metadata, fail without deleting an extension.
episode.diff: The change renamed the core input concept from extensionName to extensionIdentifier; replaced the name-only existence check with lookup by normalized configured name or normalized recorded source; retained the resolved config.name as the canonical lifecycle key; generalized the not-found error; updated CLI argument documentation; and added tests proving source-URL deletion and canonical-name telemetry while preserving name-based deletion, unrelated installations, and safe failure when metadata is absent.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 2d406ffc755f79dc903c6993aae03150e1678dc0 is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 8692 and has parent 0534ca74d4e67b00ed51e9f8bf568efc3ecaf834.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller 2d406ffc755f79dc903c6993aae03150e1678dc0; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0] and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation accepted extensionName, checked only exact equality with installed.config.name, and used that input directly for enablement removal, storage selection, and telemetry.
evidence_units.source: git show 0534ca74d4e67b00ed51e9f8bf568efc3ecaf834:packages/cli/src/config/extension.ts, uninstallExtension implementation around lines 575-604

evidence_units.claim: The pinned diff replaces the exact name-only guard with a lookup whose predicates compare a lowercased identifier to both lowercased configured name and optional lowercased metadata source, returning the matching configured name.

The resulting implementation resolves the external identifier to config.name, rejects when no canonical name is found, and performs enablement removal, directory deletion, and successful-uninstall telemetry with that canonical name.
Installed extension loading reads install metadata and includes it on the loaded Extension object, providing the persisted source field used by identifier resolution.
Installation persists the installMetadata object, including its source, in the installed extension destination for supported copied installation types.

The uninstall command passes its positional argument unchanged to uninstallExtension, so identifier interpretation is owned by the lifecycle implementation rather than duplicated in the command handler.
The command-line positional argument description was broadened from extension name to extension name or source path.
The update lifecycle still invokes uninstallExtension with the configured extension name, demonstrating that name-based internal callers remain supported.

The source-URL test creates an installed extension with git source metadata, uninstalls using that URL, verifies the installed directory is gone, and verifies telemetry uses the canonical configured name.
The missing-metadata test supplies a URL for an installed extension without install metadata and expects 'Extension not found.', proving absent provenance is not guessed from the configured name.
Existing tests verify uninstall by configured name, preservation of unrelated extensions, not-found behavior, and successful telemetry by configured name.
The extension test fixture writes install metadata only when explicitly provided, allowing the suite to distinguish provenance-backed source resolution from installations lacking provenance.

The CLI package declares Vitest as its test runner and exposes a 'vitest run' package test command; no successful local execution result was available from the checkout because its working tree contents were already removed.

candidate_atomics.name: declare-alternate-lifecycle-identifier
candidate_atomics.title: Declare the alternate identifier accepted by the lifecycle command
candidate_atomics.description: Expose that the destructive lifecycle operation accepts either the installed object's configured name or its persisted installation source, while leaving identifier interpretation in the lifecycle owner.

semantic_action.intent: Let callers intentionally request removal using the same source value used to install an object, without requiring them to discover its configured name first.
semantic_action.pre_state: The command contract describes only a configured name even though installations may retain a distinct source identifier.
semantic_action.post_state: The command contract states that a configured name or recorded source path may identify the removal target, and the raw value is forwarded to the lifecycle owner.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the command argument description and forwarding call to confirm the broadened input contract and single ownership of resolution.

candidate_atomics.name: resolve-removal-identifier-to-canonical-identity
candidate_atomics.title: Resolve a removal identifier to the canonical installed identity
candidate_atomics.description: Search installed objects by normalized canonical name or normalized persisted source, then perform all destructive and reporting operations with the matched canonical name.

semantic_action.intent: Remove the intended installed extension when the request supplies either its configured name or its persisted installation source, without deleting an unproven target.
semantic_action.module_role: installed-extension lifecycle identity resolver and removal owner
semantic_action.pre_state: A removal request contains an external identifier, while installed records have a canonical configured name and may have a distinct persisted source; the prior implementation recognizes only an exact configured name.
semantic_action.post_state: A matching installed record is resolved case-insensitively by configured name or recorded source, its configured name becomes the sole key for enablement cleanup, storage deletion, and telemetry, and requests with no evidenced match fail before removal.
semantic_action.validation: Test removal by source and assert directory deletion plus canonical-name telemetry; test name-based removal and preservation of unrelated installations; test that an unmatched source or an installation without metadata returns not found.

candidate_workflows.name: support-provenance-based-extension-removal
candidate_workflows.title: Support safe removal by configured identity or recorded installation source
candidate_workflows.description: Broaden a lifecycle removal boundary to accept a provenance identifier, resolve it against installed state, and preserve one canonical identity for cleanup and reporting.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow an installed extension to be safely uninstalled using either its configured name or the source recorded at installation, while keeping deletion and telemetry anchored to the canonical configured name.
when_to_use: A lifecycle command accepts only an internal or configured name, but users retain and naturally reuse the source URL or path supplied during installation.
Installed records persist provenance that can unambiguously identify the lifecycle target.
Existing cleanup subsystems require a canonical installed name rather than the external identifier.
anti_goals: Do not infer a source match from URL fragments, directory names, or configured-name similarity when persisted provenance is absent.
Do not pass a source URL or path directly into storage deletion, enablement-state removal, or telemetry as though it were the canonical installed name.
Do not broaden the change into installation, update, reload, or storage-layout redesign.
Do not remove unrelated installed extensions while resolving the requested identifier.
not_applicable_when: Installation provenance is not persisted or loaded into the installed-object model.
Multiple installed records can legitimately share the same source and no disambiguation policy exists.
The removal backend already uses an immutable identifier that callers possess, making alternate identity reconciliation unnecessary.
inputs: Removal identifier supplied by the caller
Configured canonical name for each installed record
Optional persisted installation source for each installed record
Existing enablement, storage-removal, and telemetry mechanisms
workflow_graph.entry_state: The requested identifier may be a configured name or installation source, installed records are loadable, and the removal mechanisms operate on configured names; source-only requests are not yet recognized.
workflow_graph.exit_state: A request matching a configured name or recorded source removes exactly the matched extension and reports its canonical configured name; a request without an evidenced match fails before lifecycle state or storage is removed.

steps.condition: The public removal command is intended to accept the persisted installation source in addition to the configured name.
steps.validation: The argument help names both accepted identifier forms, and the command forwards the unmodified identifier to the lifecycle owner.

steps.condition: Installed records expose canonical names and optional persisted sources.
steps.validation: Source-based and name-based tests delete the intended directory; telemetry receives the canonical name; unrelated installations remain; absent metadata and unmatched identifiers produce not-found failure.

validation_ladder: Static contract check: confirm the public argument description includes configured name and source, and resolution remains centralized in the lifecycle implementation.
Resolver check: confirm matching covers normalized configured name and optional normalized persisted source and returns the configured name.
Negative unit check: confirm an unmatched identifier and a source request against an installation without metadata fail before deletion.
Positive unit check: confirm removal by configured name and by persisted source deletes the intended installed directory.
Isolation check: confirm another installed extension remains after removal.
Side-effect identity check: confirm enablement cleanup, storage selection, and telemetry use the resolved canonical configured name.
Regression check: confirm internal name-based lifecycle callers, including update replacement, remain compatible.
stop_conditions: Stop if installed records do not expose persisted source metadata; do not invent source identity from names or paths.
Stop if source identity is ambiguous across installed records until a disambiguation contract is established.
Stop and fail safely if neither canonical name nor recorded source matches the request.
Stop extraction-level validation claims short of asserting a successful local test run, because only the committed test oracle—not an execution result—was available in this checkout.
unresolved_or_deferred: The committed tests demonstrate exact source-string matching but do not explicitly execute mixed-case name or source inputs, even though the implementation lowercases both operands.
The behavior for duplicate installed records with the same recorded source is unspecified; Array.find would select the first loaded record.
The CLI success message echoes the caller-supplied identifier rather than the resolved canonical name; the change does not establish whether that presentation is intentional.
A local Vitest result is unavailable because the provided checkout's tracked working-tree files were already deleted; validation is grounded in committed test code rather than a fresh execution.

unresolved_questions: Does the product guarantee uniqueness of installMetadata.source across installed extensions, or should source-based removal detect and reject ambiguity?
Should source identifiers receive path or URL canonicalization beyond case folding, such as trailing-slash, .git-suffix, relative-path, or platform-specific path normalization?
Should the command's positional variable be renamed from 'name' to 'identifier' or its success output use the resolved canonical name?
The issue bundle lacks PR body, review discussion, and status-check results, so design rationale and CI execution status cannot be independently established.
